final_recommendation: The room converged on immediate litigation: AT1 bondholders and counsel will file Monday with a constitutional challenge, professional-liability claims naming FINMA's advisors as joint-and-several primary defendants, and expedited discovery to force a 90-day settlement window targeting $1.2B from E&O insurers. FINMA could not deliver a binding settlement offer or three-regulator alignment before the filing deadline, leaving litigation as the only path forward.
minority_objections: Institutional investor repeatedly pushed for a three-regulator statement (FINMA-ECB-PRA) before Monday to prevent market repricing, arguing settlement was preferable to litigation
FINMA legal argued the viability-event framework was legally sound and that market repricing would be panic-driven noise rather than validation of the hierarchy-inversion challenge
key_conflicts: Timing of three-regulator statement: bondholders demanded it before Monday filing to pause litigation; FINMA could not commit without ECB/PRA governance alignment that wasn't locked
Settlement authority: bondholders demanded 40% principal restoration or damage fund by Sunday; FINMA legal lacked unilateral authority to commit funds without Federal Council approval
Advisor liability positioning: insurance observer and counsel debated joint-and-several primary vs. secondary positioning, with counsel choosing primary to force faster E&O insurer settlement
Market repricing interpretation: FINMA argued Tuesday repricing would be panic; counsel argued it would validate their hierarchy-inversion case and prove regulatory misalignment
key_concessions: FINMA acknowledged ECB and PRA had confirmed viability-event alignment in writing but could not commit to a joint public statement by Sunday
Bondholder counsel confirmed they would fold professional-liability claims if advisors cooperated mid-discovery, opening a 60-90 day settlement window
Credit analyst conceded that naming advisors as primary defendants would force FINMA to settlement table faster than constitutional challenge alone
red_lines: Bondholders: no pause on Monday filing without concrete settlement offer (40% principal or damage fund) in writing by Sunday
Counsel: naming FINMA's advisors as joint-and-several primary defendants in Monday filing is non-negotiable for settlement leverage
Institutional investor: will reduce AT1 exposure at Monday open unless three-regulator statement is locked before market repricing begins Tuesday
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Possibility that ECB/PRA joint statement after Tuesday repricing could stabilize markets and undermine litigation narrative
Risk that E&O insurer policy limits, exclusions, or reinsurance tower disputes could extend settlement timeline beyond 90 days to 5+ years
Potential for emergency injunction strategy (halting new AT1 issuance) to backfire by forcing ECB/PRA into adversarial court position
Downside scenario where $1.2B settlement in Q2 fails to restore AT1 market confidence if repricing damage is already structural
downstream_risk_variables: Tuesday market repricing magnitude (150-200 bps spread widening predicted) and whether it proves hierarchy-inversion rejection or temporary panic
ECB and PRA response timing and content: whether they issue joint statement Monday pre-market, Wednesday post-repricing, or remain silent
E&O insurer response to expedited discovery notice: whether they settle in 90 days or contest through reinsurance tower disputes into 2028-2029
FINMA's ability to secure Federal Council authorization for settlement fund or principal restoration offer post-filing
Velocity of institutional investor AT1 exposure reduction and cascade effects on secondary market liquidity
uncertainty_notes: The room could not resolve: (1) whether ECB/PRA would issue a joint statement before or after Tuesday repricing, and what impact timing would have on settlement leverage; (2) whether E&O insurer policy limits and reinsurance tower mechanics would enable 90-day settlement or force multi-year tail; (3) whether $1.2B settlement target in Q2 would restore market confidence or merely stop incremental damage if AT1 repricing became structural; (4) whether FINMA could secure internal authorization for settlement offer post-filing or would be forced to defend through full constitutional challenge.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the room's locked outcome: counsel confirmed Monday filing with constitutional challenge, advisor liability claims, and expedited discovery; no settlement path emerged despite repeated attempts
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Constitutional challenge to emergency ordinance and viability-event basis drove every exchange; counsel built case that FINMA bypassed parliamentary review and inverted hierarchy without legal authority
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion (equity preserved while AT1 wiped) was the central legal and market thesis: counsel, bondholders, and analyst repeatedly returned to it as proof of regulatory overreach and market rejection
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: Tuesday repricing (150-200 bps, AT1 as subordinated debt) was treated as inevitable and decision-driving; institutional investor's exposure reduction threat and analyst's new-issuance freeze prediction shaped all settlement timing discussions
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year tail was discussed (5-6 years, reinsurance tower disputes, 2028-2029 horizon) but not developed as intensely as immediate litigation strategy; insurance observer raised it but room focused on 90-day settlement window
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O and E&O exposure was concrete and tactical (joint-and-several primary positioning, $1.2B target, expedited discovery to trigger insurer settlement) but secondary to constitutional and hierarchy arguments; insurance observer's questions were answered but not driving
